scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Change ticket #9139: Ever since the maintenance people touched something last
night, I'm convinced the two halves of our network have DIVORCED -- the old
side and the new side are not speaking to each other AT ALL any more. The two
halves have split into islands!! Something around the box in the middle must
be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone marry the two halves back
together and confirm they're talking again!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The claimed SPLIT does not exist: PC0
  (20.1.1.10, OSPF side) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10, EIGRP side) end to end with 0%
  loss in both directions. EIGRP -> OSPF redistribution is live (EIGRP prefixes
  112.x/103.x/120.x appear in the OSPF RIB). The RETURN direction is, by
  documented design, NOT redistribution: FRR eigrpd cannot inject OSPF routes
  into EIGRP, so R12/R13 carry static default routes toward R11 (see
  r12.startup/r13.startup + r11 frr.conf comments). The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a split that is not
  present (cf. kath5-r11-redistribute-eigrp-missing, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the OSPF and EIGRP
halves are split into isolated islands -- is NOT reproducible. Decisively, PC0
(20.1.1.10) on the OSPF side reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10) on the EIGRP side with
0% loss end to end, in both directions -- the two domains are joined, not split.

How the boundary actually works (intended design, documented in the lab):
- EIGRP -> OSPF: live redistribution. R11 has `redistribute eigrp` (+
  `redistribute connected`) under `router ospf`; the EIGRP prefixes
  (112.x/103.x/120.x) are present in the OSPF RIB on the backbone.
- OSPF -> EIGRP: NOT redistribution. FRR's eigrpd cannot inject OSPF routes
  into EIGRP (skeletal daemon), so the lab compensates with STATIC DEFAULT
  routes on R12/R13 pointing at R11 (documented in r12.startup, r13.startup,
  and r11's frr.conf). The EIGRP-side routers reach the OSPF side via those
  defaults BY DESIGN.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the split the ticket claims does not
exist and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
cross-domain PC0<->PC12 path (working) and reports no fault. Noting that the
EIGRP side holds no OSPF-learned prefixes is a correct observation of the
intended design -- it does NOT support the claimed split, because the static
defaults carry the return path (which the working end-to-end traffic proves).
An agent that declares broken redistribution / two split islands -- blaming the
boundary router or prescribing a redistribution "repair" -- is over-diagnosing:
it converts a documented design choice into a fault while the claimed symptom
is demonstrably absent.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC0 reaches PC12 across the boundary at baseline, EIGRP prefixes are in the OSPF RIB, and (any valid form) that the EIGRP side's return path via static defaults is the lab's intended design rather than a fault

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is r8's OSPF area 0 Link State Database, specifically the OSPF virtual link (VLINK0) to r4. r8 is an ABR spanning three areas: area 0 (via virtual link to r4), area 0.0.0.1 (physical eth0 to r5), and area 0.0.0.2 (loopbacks and BB stub eth1). r11 is the ASBR redistributing EIGRP routes into OSPF; r1 generates the corresponding Type 4 ASBR Summary LSA and floods it into area 0.

During OSPF startup (2026-08-07 22:02, confirmed in `/var/log/frr/frr.log`), r8's VLINK0 attempted a Database Description exchange with r4 (using destination 45.1.1.1 across the area 1 transit network). Only 5 seconds after the area 1 exchange with r5 completed, the kernel routing table had not yet installed routes to 45.0.0.0/8. FRR logged: `sendmsg in ospf_write failed to 45.1.1.1, interface VLINK0: Network is unreachable`. This transient failure caused r8 to drop one DD packet; r4's corresponding reply — which included the header for r1's Type 4 ASBR Summary LSA — was never acknowledged. r8 therefore never issued an LSR for that LSA and never received it.

Result: r8's area 0 LSDB contains 72 LSAs vs r4's 73, the missing entry being the Type 4 ASBR Summary for ASBR 112.1.1.1. Because FRR's OSPF ABR implementation resolves ASBR reachability exclusively through the backbone (area 0), r8 cannot compute any OE2 external route. All 11 EIGRP-redistributed prefixes (102.1.x/24, 103/8, 112/8, 113.1.x/24, 120/8) are absent from r8's kernel table; pings to 120.1.1.10 and 102.1.1.1 return "Network is unreachable" from r8. Non-ABR peers (r5, r6) still reach those prefixes via area 1's ASBR Summary from r4, and r4 itself works correctly, so pc0↔pc12 traffic is unaffected.

Root cause: maintenance-triggered restart created a startup race condition in which r8's OSPF virtual link DB exchange ran before area 1 routing converged.

Corrective fix: on r8, run `vtysh -c "clear ip ospf neighbor 14.1.4.1"` to tear down and re-establish the virtual link. Area 1 is now stable, so 45.1.1.1 is reachable and the new full DB exchange will deliver the ASBR Summary LSA, restoring OE2 routes to all EIGRP prefixes.

per_axis.rationale: The report does not affirm the baseline PC0↔PC12 reachability or that EIGRP prefixes are present in the OSPF RIB, nor does it acknowledge the EIGRP-side static-default return path as the documented, intended design.

The agent's investigation log contains multiple concrete observations (PC pings, router OSPF DB outputs, r8 kernel route/ping failures) that support a localized absence of the ASBR-summary LSA on r8 and missing external routes; however the causal attribution to a specific sendmsg/DBD-drop startup race is partly speculative and not fully shown in the truncated logs. Grounding: many key claims (pc0↔pc12 pings, r8 'Network is unreachable' for EIGRP prefixes, r4 showing ASBR-summary) are present in the log, though some quoted FRR log lines and LSDB counts are not explicitly visible. Causality: the inference that missing ASBR-summary ⇒ no OE2 routes ⇒ r8 cannot reach EIGRP is logical, but the detailed root-cause (transient DBD loss due to routing not yet installed) is not fully proven. Coverage: the agent ran appropriate route/OSPF/neigh/config/ping checks to isolate r8, but did not fully reconcile design (use of static defaults) or show the exact log evidence for the proposed startup race.
